subject: Post-call: DPA & SCC pathing + who is controller vs processor (ProspectX)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@prospectx.com>, Samuel Green <samuel.green@prospectx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: DPA & SCC pathing + who is controller vs processor (ProspectX)

Hi Marta / Sam — thanks for the time today, great to walk through the integration goals. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary from call:
- ProspectX intends to send user-provided content to Redwood for inference; expected retention: transient (no persistent user datastore).
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, signed DPA, and SCCs for EU-involved processing later in the year.
- Security questionnaire: ProspectX will send their vendor questionnaire back to us for completion.

Open questions we flagged (please confirm):
1) Controller/Processor roles: Is ProspectX confirming they will be the Controller and Redwood the Processor for the integration? (That was our understanding but want it on record.)
2) SCC path: do you have a preference for the SCC module style (e.g., Module 2 / Controller-to-Processor vs Module 3)? If you don’t have a preference we can propose Module 2 as the typical Controller-to-Processor flow.
3) Timeline: what target date do you have for legal to finish DPA review? We can typically turn around a DPA draft within 3–5 business days after receiving any redlines from your counsel.

Attachments I’m sending now: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (DPA template), Redwood_SCC_options_matrix.docx (short comparison). I’ve also included Aditya and Neha on this thread to help drive any SCC/legal questions and to collect SOC 2 artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
- Marta: confirm controller/processor roles in reply and share the vendor questionnaire (we have a copy below but please attach the final).
- We’ll complete the questionnaire and return it along with a DPA signed or with tracked redlines, and include our SOC 2 report.
- Internal: Aditya to recommend SCC module and call out any non-standard clauses; Neha to prepare a SOC 2 evidence package.

If that aligns, reply with preferred timeline and attach the questionnaire. Thanks — looking forward to moving to legal review.

—
Lauren Bishop
Principal Solutions Executive
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
(555) 425-0193
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@prospectx.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Green <samuel.green@prospectx.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T16:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA & SCC pathing + who is controller vs processor (ProspectX)

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below:

1) Controller/Processor: correct — ProspectX will be Controller; Redwood will be Processor. We’ll need the DPA to reflect Controller-to-Processor relationship.
2) SCC module: for now we prefer Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor). If Redwood has strong recommendations to the contrary, please outline them.
3) Timeline: our legal team would like the DPA and questionnaire returned within 3 weeks (target m/d: 2026-09-16). That gives us time for an internal review and a single round of redlines. If you can prioritize SOC 2 evidence (summary report + most recent Type II date), that will speed review.

I’ve attached the vendor questionnaire — filename: ProspectX_vendor_questionnaire.xlsx. Expect Samuel (security) and I to review Redwood’s responses; Samuel will reach out if he needs to follow up.

A couple of notes:
- We asked about data residency for EU customers; while our initial scope is US-only, we may expand to EU next quarter. Please call out any SCC implications in your recommendation.
- We’ll also run a short privacy review — please confirm that subcontracting (if Redwood uses third-party processors) is covered under the DPA and that a subprocessors list will be provided.

Thanks — Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Legal Ops, ProspectX
marta.lopez@prospectx.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@prospectx.com>, Samuel Green <samuel.green@prospectx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA & SCC pathing + who is controller vs processor (ProspectX)

Perfect, thanks Marta — that helps a lot. We’ll proceed on Module 2 as the default and will call out differences for EU expansion.

What we’re doing next (internal owners included):
- Aditya: I’ve asked you to review the SCC options and recommend a single draft for Module 2 (highlight any clauses that typically get redlined). Please prepare the redline-ready SCC module and short rationale by EOD 2026-08-28.
- Neha: please prepare the SOC 2 package (summary report PDF, scope statement, and date of most recent Type II) to attach to the questionnaire responses.
- I’ll complete the vendor questionnaire we received and attach the DPA draft for your legal review.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (attached), Redwood_SCC_options_matrix.docx (attached).

Marta — I’ll send the completed questionnaire with links to SOC 2 materials by 2026-08-28 so you have a week to circulate internally before your 2026-09-16 target. If we hit any blockers, I’ll escalate to Vivek.

—
Lauren
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T20:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA & SCC pathing + who is controller vs processor (ProspectX)

Lauren — clear. I’ll take the SCC module work. Initial notes:
- Module 2 is appropriate for the Controller->Processor model (ProspectX controller).
- Watchpoints: security carve-outs around logging/monitoring, subprocessors list & audit rights, breach notification SLA timing, and deletion/return of data language. I’ll draft language that favors standard Processor obligations but call out anything that might be a negotiation knob (e.g., shortened notification windows).
- I’ll attach a redline-ready SCC module (word doc) and a 1-page rationale. ETA: 2026-08-28 17:00 PDT.

Neha — once I have the SCC redline I’ll mark any additional evidence requests you should prep for SOC 2. Vivek — FYI in case we need legal escalation for non-standard customer asks.

—Aditya
